topic.title: Sinusoidal Function Context and Data Modeling
topic.summary: Building sinusoidal models of periodic phenomena: the period from consecutive maximums or minimums, the amplitude and midline from the extreme values, the phase shift from one data point, sinusoidal regression, and where a model can be trusted.

variants.stem: The function T models the temperature in a desert town, in degrees Fahrenheit, where t is measured in hours after midnight. It is sinusoidal. Its maximum value, 6.6 degrees, occurs at t = 6, and its next minimum value, 1.2 degrees, occurs at t = 13.

parts.prompt: Find the period of T.
Find the amplitude of T.
Find the midline value d, so that the midline is y = d.

solution: From a maximum to the next minimum is half a cycle: 13 − 6 = 7. The period is 2(7) = 14.
The amplitude is half the difference of the extreme values: (6.6 − 1.2)/2 = 2.7.
The midline is the mean of the extreme values: (6.6 + 1.2)/2 = 3.9.
